subject: ventures/shift-roster-builder
professional: a payroll and scheduling specialist for US hourly teams (restaurants, retail) who knows FLSA weekly overtime, California daily overtime and meal periods, and the federal 14-15 youth hour rules; first checks: what a week of shifts costs against a hand calculation, overnight shifts, minors' hours on weekends, and whether malformed input is refused rather than dropped

evidence.correctness: Recomputed six weekly costs by hand from statute through buildRoster with my own script (scratchpad pay.mjs, not the product's tests), one person at $20/h: FLSA 5x10 h = 40x20 + 10x30 = $1,100 (pass); California 13 h day with OT after 8, DT after 12 = 8x20 + 4x30 + 1x40 = $320 (pass); California 5x9 h = $950 (pass); California 6x8 h, weekly OT on hours not already premium = 40x20 + 8x30 = $1,040 (pass); 30-min unpaid meal on five 9 h shifts = 42.5 paid h = $875 (pass; my first hand figure of $850 was my own arithmetic slip, corrected). Overnight Sat 8pm-6am with daily OT after 8: $220 with 2 OT h on arrival, where calendar days give 4 h + 6 h = $200 (fail: prior defect 0 still open on main). After this PR's re-land of PR #19894: $200, 0 OT h.
evidence.completeness: Prior defects re-checked against the code on arrival: comma-less shift line now errors ('could not read the day') alone and before a valid line, while a real header row is still skipped; the youth rule gives a 15-year-old 8 h on Saturday (6 h Saturday shift filled) and keeps 3 h on a school day (Mon 4 h shift left open, correctly); the CLI disclaimer now names what is checked. Claimed '11 fair-workweek presets': FWW_PRESETS has 11 named cities plus custom (pass). Not run: browser page, server end to end, hosted hub (README itself says not deployed).
evidence.verification: node --test '*.test.mjs' on main: 787 tests, 787 pass, 0 skipped, 277 s (82 files; round 84 ran 6 of 82). Mutants: youth weekend cap 8->3 caught (calc.test.mjs); comma-less-line header test >1 -> >=1 caught (closes the verification side of prior defect 2); default otAfter 40->41 survived calc.test.mjs but caught by the full suite; meal boundary len > mealAfter -> >= survived all 787 tests (new defect, low). This PR adds a test that catches the meal mutant and pins the 40 h default in calc.test.mjs; the re-landed overnight test catches reverting the midnight split.
evidence.craft: calc.mjs is now 6,088 lines (6,076 at round 84) and README.md 543,860 bytes / 4,050 lines; the opener's 'hour of spreadsheet shuffling' line is still unmeasured (README.md:11). payParts and payPartsMap still duplicate the daily/weekly split, though the overnight split now shares slotDays. Prior defect 4 open.
evidence.claims: Disclaimer cli.mjs:665/700 now 'Checks only the scheduling-notice presets it names and the US federal limits for ages 14-15' (pass, prior defect 3 closed). 11 presets (pass). README daily-OT paragraph said a shift counts on the day it starts, which matched the code but not the timesheet; the re-land rewrites it. served-copy.mjs: no placeholder or retired origin in llms.txt, sitemap, robots, canonicals (pass). Hosted hub section says plainly it is not deployed and pricing is not set (pass).
evidence.fitness: A manager can build a week, see which shifts stay open and why, and price it under federal or California rules; before this PR a manager running overnight closes under daily overtime saw a planned cost that disagreed with the product's own timesheet.
evidence.domain: Against 29 USC 207 (weekly OT over 40), California Labor Code 510 (daily OT after 8, DT after 12, weekly OT on non-premium hours) and 512(a) (meal for more than five hours), and 29 CFR 570.35 (14-15: 3 h school day, 8 h non-school day, 18/40 h week, 7am-7pm): all modelled rules match on the cases checked. The calendar-midnight workday is a stated simplification (California lets an employer fix any 24-hour workday); the README and post now say so.

verdict: Three of round 84's six defects are closed (weekend hours for 14-15 year olds, the silently dropped comma-less shift line, the understated disclaimer) and their mutants are now caught. Five of six hand-recomputed weekly costs match statute (FLSA $1,100; California $320, $950, $1,040; meal $875); the sixth, an overnight shift under daily overtime, still cost $220 against $200 on main, because PR #19894's fix sat open and red on an unrelated test. This PR re-lands it ($200 after). The full suite now runs: 787 of 787 pass in 277 s. A seeded meal-boundary bug survived all 787 tests; this PR adds the test. It still meets the bar on correctness, claims and verification; craft stays at 2 (6,088-line module, 544 KB README), and the relative canonical is unchanged. Not run: the browser page, the server, the hosted hub.
